review_scope: Independent practical review of existing static child-friendly stylized scene props. No model changes, no new modeling, no new renders, no main publication.

findings.recognition: Clear rounded head, short closed beak, compact torso, folded wings, two standing legs and two long paired tail streamers. The paired streamers distinguish it strongly from the companion bird.
findings.silhouette: All six views preserve readable major parts. Paired streamers are separate from top/rear views and remain clear of the floor in the side view. No visible gross penetration, exposed body hole or floating major part.
findings.placement: Both feet reach the ground plane. Allow approximately 0.143 m width, 0.478 m total fore-aft depth including streamers and 0.219 m height. Keep scenery clear of the long low trailing streamers.
optional_polish: Streamers are quite fine edge-on and may disappear at distant screen sizes. This is a placement/LOD consideration, not a blocker for the current static prop.

source_opening_warning_interpretation.method: Decode GLB triangle positions; count undirected geometric edges after merging identical exact float-coordinate positions across all material meshes. Read source loft/material-batching construction as supporting evidence. This is an in-memory diagnostic, not a model edit.
source_opening_warning_interpretation.conclusion: Warnings are coincident material seams, not open holes in the combined surface. Accept for this static environment-prop scope.

packaging_issue_at_review.severity: Fix before metadata-driven preview integration; not a modeling defect
packaging_issue_at_review.status: RESOLVED: corrected metadata.preview now points to the existing hero PNG; reviewer rechecked the path and all model/image hashes.

limits: Existing six views are five color directions plus a matching hero clay view; underside and left side were not separately rendered.
No runtime viewer, Three.js import, collision, rigging or animation test was run.
Acceptance here covers the exact GLB and image hashes above; publication is a separate decision.
